identity.title: Oscillatory Integral Operators and Variable Schrödinger Propagators: Beyond the Universal Estimates

assessment: Major revision required for the stated higher-dimensional Nikodym condition and conclusions; exact v2 initial review complete.
outcome: One confirmed Major with all-hypothesis n=5 counterexample and seven confirmed local Minor findings; later independent scientific acceptance remains pending.

problems.title: Higher-dimensional Hypothesis II admits full universal compression
problems.location: Definition 2.7 pp.10-11; Proposition 4.2(II), proof pp.35-36; Theorems 2.8(II),2.9(II) p.11; compare dagger phase pp.18-20
problems.claim_type: all-hypothesis counterexample to sublevel implication and two main conclusions
problems.hypothesis_checks: n=5, polynomial real analytic phase; mixed Hessian I4; H2 follows det H'=1 and nonzero Gauss time component; inverse Psi=omega-Hy and correct origin; alpha={1,2,4}, beta={2,3,4}, d=3, constant jet rank r=2; every parameter and Taylor centre checked; Hypothesis II does not require psi(0;y)=0.
problems.witness: H=diag([[1-t^2,t],[t,0]],same); phi=x.y+y^T H y/2. All selected 19 nonempty minors lie in {0,t,t^2}; span(t,t^2) excludes 1, including all Taylor centres. Take D=I4,d(omega)=omega. I-H has rank 2 for every t, all 16 three-minors vanish, one two-minor equals 1.
problems.decisive_evidence: False expansion p.36 has constant -1 instead of -det(I_alpha,beta)=0; evaluate t=0. Compressed local 3-manifold S in R5 has delta-neighbourhood O(delta^2), forcing Nikodym norm >=c delta^(-2/p). Rank-2 stationary phase gives propagator norm >=c lambda^(1-1/q). Explicit p=4,q=5/2 contradict strict gains with epsilon smaller than the gap.
problems.actual_impact: Proposition 4.2(II), Theorems 2.8(II) and 2.9(II) fail in n=5 in this exact v2. Three-dimensional Theorem 2.4(II) and standalone analytic Propositions 5.1/5.3 are not refuted.
problems.repair: Strengthen Hypothesis II to genuine determinant/sublevel control. Directly assuming Definition 4.1 preserves only the later conditional route, subject to local corrections. Requiring principal minors alone has not been proved sufficient because arbitrary D mixes columns.
problems.repair_verification: No new sufficient weak high-dimensional condition established; exact counterexample verified analytically and with independently authored rational-polynomial calculation.

independent_acceptance.source_fidelity: Hypothesis II and Theorems 2.8/2.9, pp.10-11; sublevel application p.36; exact dagger phase pp.18-20. Definition 2.1's additional zero-base-phase condition is not imposed by II.
independent_acceptance.hypotheses_checked: n=5, H=diag(B,B), B=[[1-t^2,t],[t,0]], alpha={1,2,4}, beta={2,3,4}. H1=I, det H'=1, gradient centered at origin, local inverse Psi=omega-Hy. All 19 nonempty selected minors lie in span(t,t^2), exclude constant 1 at every center; the normalized jet determinant is 1. D=I and d(omega)=omega are admissible on equal local balls.
independent_acceptance.decisive_evidence: Actual exact calculations give rank(I-H)=2, all sixteen 3-minors zero and a 2-minor equal to 1. Thus the asserted SN small-sublevel bound fails on the full interval. Tubes lie in the 3-dimensional set x1=-t x2,x3=-t x4 with delta-neighborhood volume O(delta^2), forcing delta^(-2/p). With fhat=e^(-i lambda |y|^2/2)psi, quadratic stationary phase gives input <=lambda^(-2+4/q), output >=lambda^(-1) on volume comparable to lambda^3, and ratio lambda^(1-1/q), contradicting the claimed strict improvement for 2<q<3. The p.36 constant term is -det(I_alpha,beta)=0, not -1.
independent_acceptance.counterevidence: The phase is already correctly centered; no omitted translation normalization excludes it. Three-dimensional conclusions and analytic Propositions 5.1/5.3 under their own hypotheses are not refuted. Principal-minor restriction alone is not certified a repair because arbitrary D introduces other columns.
independent_acceptance.dependency_and_severity: False core non-compression and resulting high-dimensional estimates under stated Hypothesis II. Major supported by actual admissible counterexamples, with bounded dimension and exponent scope.
independent_acceptance.repair_scope: No replacement high-dimensional theorem or complete repair asserted.

problems.title: Kakeya non-compression index set includes the target full minor
problems.location: Definition of I(alpha,beta) and Definition 2.6 p.10; proper-minor parenthetical p.35
problems.claim_type: vacuous hypothesis due to exact index error
problems.hypothesis_checks: Applies to every translation-invariant phase as defined; the pair (alpha,beta) itself belongs to the displayed index set.
problems.witness: Coefficient of the full minor equal to 1, all others 0 makes the defining dependence true for every y,t; Z_K is the full ball.
problems.decisive_evidence: Direct substitution; source p.35 separately states intended strict cardinality restriction.
problems.actual_impact: Higher-dimensional I statements have no admissible phases as written. This is not a satisfying-hypothesis counterexample to those conditional theorems.
problems.repair: Use distinct proper-minor I_< for Kakeya and all-minor I_<= where needed for Nikodym.
problems.repair_verification: Local algebra checked: Hessian vanishes at t=0 under Definition 2.1, eliminating constant term before Proposition 5.1. Does not repair P1.

independent_acceptance.source_fidelity: Full-minor index in Hypothesis I p.10 and intended proper-minor expansion p.35.
independent_acceptance.hypotheses_checked: The index set includes the pair alpha,beta of full selected size.
independent_acceptance.decisive_evidence: The coefficient of that same minor can be 1 and all others 0, putting the target in its own span. The stated non-membership cannot hold.
independent_acceptance.counterevidence: This makes the hypothesis vacuous; it is not an example satisfying I with a false conclusion.
independent_acceptance.dependency_and_severity: Local indexing defect; intended proper-minor formulation is explicitly visible later. Minor.
independent_acceptance.repair_scope: Use separate proper/full minor index sets and the stated zero-base-phase normalization for this expansion. Does not repair P1.

problems.title: Local inverse centred at omega=0 is not implied by H1
problems.hypothesis_checks: n=3, phi=x.y+t|y|^2+100y1; real analytic, H1=I2, H2 nonsingular.
problems.witness: Throughout D, partial_y1 phi=x1+2ty1+100>97, so cannot equal omega1 in a ball of radius rho<1 around zero.
problems.decisive_evidence: Exact gradient inequality independent of shrinking rho.
problems.actual_impact: Curves as centred in (1.3) need not exist without a normalization.
problems.repair: Centre omega at the actual gradient or subtract its linear frequency term before shrinking the inverse-function patch.
problems.repair_verification: Mixed Hessian and curvature unchanged; modulation or input translation preserves relevant norms. P1 already satisfies the missing centering.

independent_acceptance.source_fidelity: Local inverse-branch definition near zero in the early curve definitions, pp.6-8.
independent_acceptance.hypotheses_checked: phi=x.y+t|y|^2+100y1 satisfies H1 and H2 on the displayed local domains.
independent_acceptance.decisive_evidence: The first y-gradient coordinate exceeds 97 there, so a branch for omega near 0 cannot exist as written.
independent_acceptance.counterevidence: Subtracting the constant linear y term or centering omega at the actual gradient restores the local inverse and preserves relevant operator norms.
independent_acceptance.dependency_and_severity: Missing normalization with direct local repair, Minor. P1 satisfies the normalization already.
independent_acceptance.repair_scope: Center at the actual gradient; no new theorem proof claimed.

problems.title: Wrong middle sign in Example 3.1 Jacobian
problems.location: Section 3.1 p.16 formula for J Phi and A,B,C
problems.hypothesis_checks: Use admissible smooth omega(y)=y, y=0,t=1/4 with nonzero denominator.
problems.witness: Actual determinant of Domega-diag(t,t/(1-ty2)) is 9/16; printed At^2+Bt+C gives 25/16.
problems.decisive_evidence: Symbolic expansion yields At^2-Bt+C and exact rational arithmetic independently executed.
problems.actual_impact: General Jacobian identity false; special A=B=C=0 example remains valid.
problems.repair_verification: Direct determinant expansion and rational witness agree; no claim whole example fails.

independent_acceptance.hypotheses_checked: The relevant Hessian is diag(t,t/(1-t y2)).
independent_acceptance.decisive_evidence: The determinant numerator is A t^2-B t+C, not A t^2+B t+C. D omega=I,y=0,t=1/4 yields 9/16 rather than 25/16; actual exact calculation retained.
independent_acceptance.counterevidence: The intended identically zero example has A=B=C=0, so its consequence survives.

problems.title: Compact selection and inverse-polynomial assertions do not follow
problems.location: Section 4.1 Step 3 p.26; after (4.18) p.29; Corollary A.5/Lemma A.6 p.82
problems.hypothesis_checks: Compact semialgebraic input does not force compact one-point section; nonzero Jacobian of a polynomial map does not make its inverse polynomial.
problems.witness: Compact double-cover A={(a,d) in C^2:d=a^2,1/4<=|a|<=1/2} cannot have a compact one-point-per-fibre section, since it would be continuous and imply 2k=1 on pi1. Polynomial D(z)=z^2/2,P(z)=z/2 gives inverse-composed sqrt(y/2)-ty.
problems.decisive_evidence: Primary Katz-Rogers Lemma 2.2 supplies semialgebraicity without compactness. Fundamental-group obstruction and explicit inverse formula disprove the two invoked general inferences.
problems.actual_impact: Specific parametrization/BÃ©zout proof steps lack stated justification; no full phase-induced tube-family counterexample or false final non-concentration theorem claimed.
problems.repair: Use closure in a closed containment set, finite parametrization and projected-measure pigeonhole. Keep original polynomial parameters plus frozen-coordinate constraints for BÃ©zout.
problems.repair_verification: Closure preserves semialgebraic dimension/complexity; at counted roots the square original-variable system has nonsingular Jacobian, hence isolated complex roots. Other Taylor/volume steps not newly proved by this repair.

independent_acceptance.source_fidelity: Semialgebraic section and inverse-composed polynomial claims, pp.25-29; Katz-Rogers v3 p.3.
independent_acceptance.hypotheses_checked: Compact set A={(a,d):d=a^2,1/4<=|a|<=1/2} projects onto an annulus. The cited lemma supplies a semialgebraic section without compactness. Invertible polynomial maps can have nonpolynomial inverses.
independent_acceptance.decisive_evidence: A compact section would be a continuous square-root branch on the annulus, contradicting winding degree 2k=1. D(z)=z^2/2 and P(z)=z/2 on a nonzero-Jacobian interval produce sqrt(y/2)-ty, not a polynomial.
independent_acceptance.counterevidence: Taking closure within a closed bounded containing set preserves semialgebraic dimension; finite parametrizations can be selected by projected measure. Bezout can be applied in the original variables with the auxiliary constraints and nonsingular isolated roots, instead of to the inverse composition.
independent_acceptance.dependency_and_severity: Two false local justifications admit identifiable local repairs. Minor; no claimed full new tube lemma proof.
independent_acceptance.repair_scope: Use closure/finite projected charts and the original-variable polynomial system with its Jacobian.

problems.title: Local transversality does not yield M1-only multilinear uniformity
problems.location: Definition 6.10 p.54; quantitative clause of Theorem 6.11 p.55
problems.claim_type: all-hypothesis counterexample to stated uniform constant dependence
problems.hypothesis_checks: n=k=p=2; each finite two-curve family is C-infinity with all derivatives finite, M1=1 independent of N; delta=c/N<nu=1/3; full nearby-core infimum is transverse on X; r=1/2.
problems.witness: gamma1=0,gamma2=sin(Nt)/N. Around O(N) zeros, choose rectangles |x|,|t-tj|<delta/8. They lie in both tubes and nearby slopes have absolute cos>0.99.
problems.decisive_evidence: LHS>=c delta sqrt(N), proposed RHS=C nu^-A delta^(1-epsilon); ratio grows N^(1/2-epsilon) for epsilon<1/2.
problems.actual_impact: M1-only uniformity false. Fixed-family bound allowing higher derivatives, and final phase-dependent estimates, not refuted by this example.
problems.repair: Allow dependence on suitable higher derivative bounds and controlled fixed-cone pieces; cited Guth Theorem 7 requires fixed-axis small slopes.
problems.repair_verification: Primary theorem scope compared to actual p.55; no first-derivative-only replacement claimed.

independent_acceptance.source_fidelity: Theorem 6.11 pp.54-55, explicit 2<=k<=n and dependence only on M1; Guth v2 p.6.
independent_acceptance.hypotheses_checked: Allowed n=k=p=2, curves gamma1=0,gamma2=sin(Nt)/N, delta=c/N. Each N is smooth with first derivative <=1; rectangles near approximately N zeros lie in both tubes and in the required ball, with tangent wedge bounded below in all specified nearby core points.
independent_acceptance.decisive_evidence: The norm over the union is comparable to delta sqrt(N), whereas the claimed bound is C delta^(1-epsilon) for fixed nu. The ratio grows like N^(1/2-epsilon).
independent_acceptance.counterevidence: Higher derivatives grow with N. This does not refute a fixed-phase estimate allowed to depend on those derivatives. Guth's actual fixed cone-axis condition is stronger than the local-X condition.
independent_acceptance.dependency_and_severity: False stronger uniform-constant assertion, isolated from a fixed-phase use. Minor.
independent_acceptance.repair_scope: State and justify adequate geometric/derivative dependence; no M1-only repair certified.

problems.title: Shrinking-cap symbol derivative sign and packet centering
problems.location: Proposition 9.1 p.73; packet definition p.74; Lemmas 9.2-9.3 p.75
problems.claim_type: false existential symbol assertion plus local modulation inconsistency
problems.hypothesis_checks: Compact cap support O(R^-1/2), negative derivative bounds at every order imply sup|a_theta|=O_L(R^-L). Fixed normalized constant phase, nonzero smooth amplitude, fixed f, lambda=R, q=2 are admissible for Proposition 9.1.
problems.witness: Taylor from outside support forces proposed symbols rapidly small; polynomially many caps and polynomial output volume cannot dominate a nonzero fixed-ball LHS of (9.3). Positive modulation in f_T also fails to produce the recentered phase difference.
problems.decisive_evidence: Exact scaling contradiction to existence, and explicit corrected algebra h=e^(i phi_lambda(zB))f, f_T=e^(-i phi_lambda(zB))h_theta,omega.
problems.actual_impact: Printed Proposition 9.1 symbol class cannot supply claimed estimate; packet normalization inconsistent. This is locally repairable and not a separate counterexample to main estimates.
problems.repair: Use positive derivative powers R^(|beta|/2), lambda^(|beta|/2), correct opposite modulation, and basepoint zB/lambda in unit phase.
problems.repair_verification: Necessary scale correction and packet identity proved; full corrected reverse square function proof not supplied. Unit-size symbols are not claimed to satisfy printed negative bounds in Lemma 9.2.

independent_acceptance.source_fidelity: Proposition 9.1 and adjacent packet formulae pp.73-75.
independent_acceptance.hypotheses_checked: Caps have diameter O(R^-1/2), but the displayed derivatives decay as R^-|beta|/2 for all orders.
independent_acceptance.decisive_evidence: Taylor expansion from outside the support forces arbitrary-power small amplitudes. For a fixed nonzero compactly supported input and the constant phase at lambda=R, the existential packet conclusion cannot reconstruct a nonzero local output. Correct decomposition is h=e^(i phi_lambda(zB;.))f, then fT=e^(-i phi_lambda(zB;.))hT, with the centered phase difference.
independent_acceptance.counterevidence: A unit amplitude is not an example satisfying the erroneous all-order derivative hypothesis. The adjacent page supplies the intended positive derivative exponent. Physical zB must be divided by lambda inside the unit-scale phase.
independent_acceptance.dependency_and_severity: Local scaling and phase-sign errors with explicit corrections; Minor.
independent_acceptance.repair_scope: Use R^(+|beta|/2), the negative restoring phase and zB/lambda. Full corrected reverse-square-function proof not asserted.

problems.title: Whitney separation and summation range missing in local-to-global proof
problems.claim_type: local geometric and summation proof errors
problems.hypothesis_checks: Disjoint dyadic siblings may have zero distance; lemma permits n=3,s=2,alpha=1/2, for which constant-phase local L-infinity to L2 bound holds.
problems.witness: Q1=[0,1),Q2=[1,2) have same parent and distance zero, with product analogues. At stated n,s,alpha, large-k term min(sigma^-2,2^k) has divergent sum.
problems.decisive_evidence: Exact interval distance and geometric-series computation.
problems.actual_impact: Scale kernel deduction and direct summation are invalid as printed; no false global conclusion asserted.
problems.repair: Use non-neighbour Whitney pairs with neighbouring parents; split alpha>=alpha_H to universal estimate and apply the series only below alpha_H.
problems.repair_verification: For n>=3,2<=s<=q(n), s alpha<s alpha_H=(n+1)/2-s(n-1)/4<=1<=(n-1)/2 ensures strict convergence; equality n=3,s=2 belongs to universal branch.

independent_acceptance.source_fidelity: Whitney decomposition p.79 and series (9.24) p.80.
independent_acceptance.hypotheses_checked: Disjoint dyadic siblings may be adjacent with zero distance. Large-k convergence requires s alpha<(n-1)/2.
independent_acceptance.decisive_evidence: Adjacent intervals [0,1),[1,2) violate the asserted comparable separation. n=3,s=2,alpha=1/2 is within the stated local range but gives terms min(sigma^-2,2^k), so the series diverges.
independent_acceptance.counterevidence: A divergent proof bound is not a counterexample to the global lemma. For the required odd-dimensional application, alpha>=alpha_H is supplied by the universal theorem; below alpha_H, s alpha<s alpha_H=(n+1)/2-s(n-1)/4<=1<=(n-1)/2, giving the strict convergence range.
independent_acceptance.dependency_and_severity: Repairable local geometry and range split; Minor.
independent_acceptance.repair_scope: Use non-neighbor cubes with neighboring parents and split off the universal-estimate range. No broader all-dimension repair asserted.

limitations: Only exact arXiv v2 audited; no version-of-record equivalence asserted.
Three-dimensional Nikodym theorem and standalone analytic sublevel propositions not refuted by P1.
Two primary references read fully; not all external books and cited proofs newly read.
No sufficient weak replacement for high-dimensional Hypothesis II, complete corrected reverse square function proof, or M1-only curved replacement established.
No author code executed; absence of code not a mathematical defect.
Product UI attribution comes from controller; runtime is GPT-6 Astra Pro and backend equivalence was not independently established.
repair_verification: Report individually proves exact local index, centering, Jacobian, selection/Bezout, packet and range corrections. Principal-minor restriction alone is not certified as a repair of P1. Local repairs do not imply whole-paper correctness or independent acceptance.
